findings.message:
[P2] Derive refill amounts from credits, not net balance deltas

When a refill occurs between retained samples while the account is being consumed, `sample.balance_quota - previous.balance_quota` is the refill minus intervening debits, not the refill amount; `baseline_quota` may remain unchanged as well. Treating that net as `amountQuota` underestimates or misses the refill, which can make the calculated rate fall below burn and report exhaustion when the refill is actually sustainable.

src/quota-projection.ts:265-269

[P2] Do not override inferred refills with stale metadata

When the provider omits `latest_refill` for a later credit, the quota state can move to an inferred adjustment while retaining the previous positive `latest_refill_amount_credits`. This code still prefers that old observation over the newer history-derived amount, so an inferred refill of a different size gets the wrong rate and exhaustion date.

src/quota-projection.ts:318-320

summary: The refill-aware projection is wired into the admin endpoint, but two amount-selection paths can produce incorrect rates and exhaustion dates.

evidence: src/quota-projection.ts adds retained-history refill event detection and a refill-aware projection that reports sustainable, no-refill, and with-refill outcomes while preserving the existing no-refill estimate.
src/admin/kernel.ts passes the retained balance history into projectPaidFallbackRunway, exposing the refill-aware fields through the quota-projection endpoint.
